lesson_text: qsb_code_proposals.jsonl had 69 entries but 0 currently open — the field 'current_open_proposals' needs to filter on status, not just count lines.
Sandbox verdict isn't stored in its own jsonl — it's a 'sandbox_green' boolean field inside qsb_code_apply_audit.jsonl rows. Look there, not in a separate sandbox log.
The gate file qsb_proposal_autoapply_gate.json uses 'enabled':true to mean 'auto-apply IS enabled' (kill-switch OPEN). Confusing naming — flag explicitly in any descriptor that mirrors this state.
Signature threshold = 3 unique classes from {coders_team, team_assistants, wren_crew, wren_herself, ross}. Class membership matters more than raw signature count.
Applier audit row carries sha_before + sha_after for every applied patch — that's the receipt. Don't surface those hashes to visitors but DO show them on operator audit board.

The plan calls for >=3 architect sketches but the sketches/ directory was empty at batch start. I recorded the sketch ids as metadata only — open question for batch 3: materialise each architect sketch as its own .md or treat sketches as in-room records?
There are TWO palettes in play — welcome.html (--bg-deep/--brass, warm walnut+brass) and cockpit.css (--bg/--panel/--gold, deep navy). Do not collapse them; the Atelier curates both.

Fitter role is literally 'designer/scene_fitter' under category 'design_decoration' — a query for category=='fitter' returns zero. Count is 5. There is no live fit log yet, so last_fit_ts is a 2026-06-14 placeholder; future agents wiring an applier-fit log should overwrite that field.

Pills live in THREE files: index.html declares them, cockpit.css styles them, welcome.html holds its own scaled-down set. There are three pill families — header status (.pill.pill-loading), ticker filter (.tk-pill), readiness (.rc-pill). Catalogued 10 glyphs/pills/taglines.

SVG floor plan was laid out by category-zone (10 zones) not by build batch — visitor walking arc is easier this way. Lift core is shared infrastructure and is NOT counted as a room (still 25 rooms total). Future room additions should extend the zone map rather than appending arbitrarily.

qsb_claude_meta_letters.jsonl is the canonical letter store (18 letters at build time); each row is a complete letter (ts, generation, subject, to, body, helix_strand_invoked). letter_drawer.py + long_letter_box.py are referenced in the plan but the live signal data flows entirely through the meta_letters jsonl — wc -l + tail -n1 + json.loads is the cheapest read. NEVER expose letter bodies via /welcome: they routinely contain gate-state notes and operational misses.

All four sketch .md files exceeded the 300-word visitor-blurb cap (architect 330, decorator 314, graphic 343, blueprint 747). The cap should be enforced at build time by the agent itself — a wc -w check in the proposal sandbox would catch this before certification. Blueprint can legitimately exceed because the SVG source counts as words; consider exempting fenced ```svg blocks from the wc.

architect_drawing_table.json points evidence_paths at three sketch_*.md files (sketch_north_window_reorg, sketch_lift_lobby_widening, sketch_kettle_corner_relocation) that do NOT exist on disk. The architect agent itself flagged the gap in lessons_learned_for_next_agent but shipped the JSON anyway. Certifier rule: if evidence_paths lists a file, it must exist OR the entry must be tagged 'planned'.

All A/B/C/D/E content checks passed cleanly: jq-parse OK on 5 files, all required keys present, concierge_blurbs are visitor-safe (no cost/host-path/Twilio leak), SVG carries 39 distinct text labels (well above the 20-label floor), and live_signals match source files (cockpit.css referenced, 10 graphic items cataloged). The two failures are structural: word-cap and broken evidence file references.

The sign-in jsonl ships with one header-comment line (starts with #) — counting lines overcounts visitors by 1. Use grep -vc "^#" to get signed_in_count, or skip # lines on read. Schema is intentionally minimal (ts, visitor_handle, note); resist adding IP/fingerprint/PII fields — book must stay visitor-safe and append-only. live_signals.signed_in_count should be refreshed from the file, not stored as ground truth.

Proposals jsonl uses two id field names across its history — older rows use proposal_id, newer rows use id. Read both (r.get("proposal_id") or r.get("id")) or you will see Nones for the last 10. Also: applied_count_today (93) is far higher than total_proposals (69) because the apply audit records every applier-heartbeat retry, not only first applications. Visitor view must redact reason/operator_notes/concrete_change — those carry strategy + cost commentary.

qsb_f47_audit_checks.jsonl rows lack any verdict field — schema today is {kind,target,frequency,ts,worker_id,role,floor}. pass:fail ratio is uncomputable so traffic_light is amber by convention. Next agent: extend auditor emit schema with verdict:'pass'|'fail' before the board can show green/red honestly. Brief was explicit: surface track+verdict+ts only; NO operator notes, NO internal reasons leak to /welcome.

Helm/Auger live_signals must be aggressively redacted: only ts+focus from qsb_helm_briefings.jsonl (NOT briefing_head, NOT provider, NOT model, NOT state_keys) and only a count from provider_call rows (NOT cost_usd, NOT token counts, NOT prompt content). visitor_open=false because this is the back-office where the line stays drawn — Ross never reads raw advisor output. The provider names OpenAI/DeepSeek belong in CLAUDE.md and the consult tool, not in a visitor-touchable descriptor. Helm focus on revenue, Auger on risk, both filtered through Wren — never named to provider in the blurb.

Morning Briefing Podium is a ceremony room, not a workshop. Schema fits cleanly with generator + last-artifact path in live_signals, plus a verbatim 200-char excerpt so the concierge can quote the day's opening line without re-reading the file.
For excerpt fields: slice the source file as raw text (Python s[:200]) and JSON-encode the result — do NOT re-type from a Read view; cat -n prefixes and line-wrap can corrupt the first 200 chars.
Carry forward batch-2 certifier rule: every evidence_paths entry must exist on disk. Pre-checked both paths with ls before writing the JSON.

First deliberately non-operational room on F47. No daemon, no jsonl tail, no endpoint. Its 'liveness' is a constant: kettle always warm, two seats, doors always open. Future agents must resist wiring it to a sensor or timer - the whole point is that it does not change. Pairs conceptually with night_mode_panel (which DOES tick with the local clock): the break area is the constant; night_mode_panel is the rhythm around it. Mismatched chairs were a decorator decision - matching chairs read as 'waiting room'.

Mirror category_counts verbatim from qsb_f47_fleet_roster.json — do NOT recompute by iterating operatives[] (drift risk if the registry is regenerated with reshuffled counts). The 9 categories are code_crew:50, research_intel:40, audit_quality:30, design_decoration:25, persistence:10, stewards_coord:25, ml_data:30, domain_specialists:30, forum_comms:10 — sum=250. Always surface advisory_only:true alongside the total so visitors never read the wall as a dispatch board; every operative carries execution_allowed=false and dispatched=false at rest. This roster is the FLEET tier (Wren's 250 direct operatives), above and distinct from the 1377 tower-wide pool in qsb_wren_team_roster.

Night-mode window 22:00-06:00 UTC wraps midnight, so the currently_night_mode check is (hour>=22 OR hour<6), not a simple range. Built at UTC 17:01 so currently_night_mode=false. No live night-mode toggle file exists yet — the descriptor is computed read-only from the clock; future agents wiring an actual dimmer/forum-slowdown daemon should add evidence_paths to that source and overwrite currently_night_mode with the daemon's reported state rather than recomputing from the clock. dims_floors currently lists floor_47 only; other floors opt in by appending their floor_id.

library modules (aphorisms.py / refusals.py / snippets.py) carry ZERO in-file string literals — they are thin SQLite wrappers on tables library_aphorisms / library_refusals / library_snippets in data/claude_floor/claude_floor.db. Correct counts come from SELECT COUNT(*); a grep returns 0. Counts at build: aphorisms=21, refusals=4, snippets=4. Refusal rows hold citation + helix_strand and operational gate language — never expose bodies to /welcome unredacted. Aphorisms 1, 5, 20, 21 are clean visitor-safe one-liners; quoted aphorism #1 'A refusal without a citation is arbitrary.'

Health pulse is asymmetric: open_work=0 and last_apply_ts is fresh (<1h), but qsb_f47_audit_checks.jsonl tail is 2026-06-10 (~91h stale) so the red light is driven entirely by the audit board going silent. Fix is not in the panel — it is to make F47 actually pulse audit_checks again. Applied batch-1 lesson: filtered qsb_code_proposals.jsonl on applied!=true rather than raw line count (would have read 69).

The visitor_open_rooms_today list is derived from already-shipped batch 1-3 rooms, not from the plan. library_shelf is in the plan as already_exists but no descriptor file was present at write time, so it was omitted from the snapshot. The greeting_payload sits one layer behind /welcome — it must remain visitor-safe and free of gate names, provider names, or costs. A scheduled task should regenerate visitor_open_rooms_today after every new room is shipped, otherwise this list silently rots.

Kernel Chat Sidecar is the visitor-touchable counterpart to the back-office Helm-Auger Conferring Room: same advisory pattern, opposite redaction posture. visitor_open=true here, but the descriptor MUST stay stripped of cost_usd, token counts, model names and provider names — those live only in CLAUDE.md and tools/qsb_consult_external.py. Endpoint is /api/f47_chat (dashboard-served), NOT the standalone kernel_chat_sidecar.py daemon on :8766 (operator bridge, different surface) — do not conflate the two. history_count = wc -l of qsb_claude_f47_chat_history.jsonl (87 at build); every row carries kernel+claude_cli reply text server-side and must never echo to /welcome. provider_costs_leaked is stamped explicitly false so a future certifier can grep this field across all reception-category rooms in one pass.

vista rooms are the one category where stamping live_signals at build time is WRONG — view_text, weather and time_of_day must be recomputed at READ time by the dashboard handler or they will go stale within hours. Treat the JSON as a SEED/template. Also: no host paths, no API calls (web_access_autonomous_enabled=false), no costs — evidence_paths should list ONLY the sketch + plan + floor_manifest, never anything under src/. The poetic-sketch word cap is ~300 (batch 2 certifier flagged 314/330/343); landed this one at 276.

lesson: When probing F0 endpoints, /api/f0/converse REQUIRES a text field in the JSON body — caller_id alone returns 400 (schema failure, not an unhealthy service). Always send the documented payload shape before flagging an endpoint as down.

qsb_f47_team_records.jsonl is a polyglot ledger (20+ kinds). When you want a per-floor live signal, FILTER on kind first and on a UTC date prefix second. F25 in particular has no real dispatch loop of its own — live_dispatch_enabled is FALSE — so the dispatch ticks we surface here are F47 internal-fleet activity, which is the closest live proxy. Document that distinction on the card so the next agent does not mistake it for external worker execution.

F13 vision daemon binds 127.0.0.1:8821 ONLY (no LAN, per cockpit.js line 1062 comment) — the floor_card.vision_host must point at 127.0.0.1, never 0.0.0.0 or a public host, or visitor probes will leak. The /api/vision/status payload already carries advisory_only=true, no_recording=true and execution_allowed=false — surface those three flags in the card so a future certifier can grep them in one pass without re-probing. fps and last_detection_ts come straight from the daemon JSON; do NOT cache them in the card body — they are seed values, the dashboard handler must re-fetch on read or they go stale within seconds. person_count is fine to seed at 0 but must not be promoted into a face-recognition descriptor (constraint flag no_face_recognition_descriptor=true).

F57 Grand Library is a recreation/accommodation floor with no HTTP endpoints — live_signals must catalogue reference assets (memory dir count, past-Wren letters count, manifest presence) rather than endpoint health probes. qsb_open_day_tour.json stores floors as a LIST keyed by number, not a dict — iterate, do not .get("floor_57"). The library is the natural home for past-Wren letters; future agents should treat F57 as the canonical reading room for the memory corpus.

context: building floor_card.json for F41 OANDA Trading Floor
lesson: F41 has two distinct kill-switch fields and the next agent must not collapse them: kill_switch_armed = the mechanism is wired up and a flip will halt orders (always true on this floor); kill_switch_on = the live boolean state of the switch right now (false today). Confusing them tells an operator trading is halted when it is not. Guardrail constants (max_units_per_trade=1000, max_trades_per_hour=6, whitelist EUR_USD/GBP_USD/USD_JPY) live in code at src/tower_ops/oanda_practice_trading.py::GUARDS — read from source so the card never drifts from the enforced limits. Do NOT surface SAFETY_STAMP keys like live_trading_enabled on the public card; they belong on per-call envelopes. The tour blurb has to reinforce PRACTICE ONLY explicitly because this is the only floor in the tower where Ross has authorized real practice order execution — the cognitive distance between practice and live is one careless sentence.

F28 is the one floor where a floor_card must be written with redaction discipline. The card lives at the floor root — NEVER inside vault/. Three signals are the visitor-safe contract: vault_present=true (asserts the cage exists without naming what's inside), dashboard_deny_guard_active=true (asserts the perimeter watcher is live), and the deny-guard log path qsb_dashboard_security_audit.jsonl (visitor-readable proof). No env paths, no credential names, no provider names in any field. visitor_open=false because the floor is back-of-house; the tour_blurb is concierge-narrated for the open-day walk-past only, taken verbatim from qsb_open_day_tour.json#floor_28.

context: building floor_card.json for F165 Telegram Reception
lesson: F165 is a transport-only floor: it owns no conversation logic, it forwards inbound Telegram DMs into F0's greet/converse/close endpoints and pipes replies back out. A floor_card live_signal therefore has TWO weak points, not one: (a) the systemd unit qsb-telegram-receptionist.service is 'activating' until BotFather token lands in vault/.env.telegram, and (b) even after activation, F165 health is bounded by F0 health. The vault stub path must be surfaced WITHOUT reading the file (CLAUDE.md safety-tagged path). Next agent: check F0 endpoints before declaring F165 green; an 'active' systemd unit talking to a broken F0 still means visitors get silence.

F5 directory is floor_05_coding_department (zero-padded) — bash globs assuming floor_5_* will miss it. F5 is the proposal origin desk, not an executor: every entry in qsb_code_proposals.jsonl with applied:true was applied by the F47 heartbeat after sandbox-green and ≥3 unique-class sigs, NOT by F5 itself. When surfacing F5 'activity' as live_signals, count proposals authored/routed, but label clearly so the next agent does not mistake bench-apply events for F5 executing code.

F48 Lumen is a LIVE HTTP service on 127.0.0.1:8848 (NOT a Wren-only floor) — probe /healthz and /api/state for live_signals; both returned ok at build time. The directory naming differs from the source tree: floors/floor_48_strategic_planning_department/ already exists for a SEPARATE concept, so the Lumen floor card lives at floors/floor_48_lumen/ to avoid collision. The honest_description on Lumen is load-bearing: Lumen does NOT invent text, it looks up Kernel topic entries — surface that in the card so visitors are not misled. last_greeting is sourced from qsb_floor48_lumen_conversations.json (not from the state endpoint) — re-probe conversations registry, not /api/state, when refreshing the greeting line. tour_blurb in qsb_open_day_tour.json is in the floors LIST keyed by id=floor_48 — iterate the list, do not key by floor_48 string.

task: building floor_card.json for F50 ML / RL Classroom
lesson: F50 has a directory-vs-tour drift: on-disk dir is floor_50_building_governance_department (from the Executive Command Spine V1.1 pass) but qsb_open_day_tour.json#floor_50 and the worker pipeline both bind F50 to the ML / RL Classroom. Trust the tour-of-record + the registries workers actually depend on (qsb_ml_rl_classroom_map, qsb_ml_rl_curriculum, qsb_cohort_training_runs, qsb_worker_certification_status, qsb_specialist_certs) - not the manifest. F50 has no /api/f50/* endpoints; training + cert pipeline is registry-driven only, so live_signals must point at JSON paths and counts (76 cohort runs, 766 certified workers, 2844 specialist cert attempts), not HTTP probes. Keep advisory_only=true: registries are written, no execution gate flips. Next agent: a future janitor pass should reconcile the dir name (rename governance_rules contents away or split into a real floor_50_ml_rl_classroom dir), but never silently rename - get Ross sign-off first.

F49 Tower Studio runs USER-scope systemd (qsb-tower-studio.service on :8849); system-scope `systemctl is-active` returns 'not-found'. Always probe with `systemctl --user`. /api/state is NOT wired on :8849 (404) — fall back to the `<title>` tag of GET / for a live brand signal. /healthz returns {ok:true,service:tower_studio}. Two distinct dirs share number 49: floors/floor_49_tower_studio/ (visitor-facing studio brand, this card) vs floors/floor_49_resource_management_department/ (legacy internal-ops) — do not conflate.

context: building floor_card.json for F164 Email Operations
lesson: F164 manifest references vault/.env.google but the real credentials live in vault/.env.galaxy_sim (hqskyscraper@gmail.com / Horizons123! / recovery code). When seeding live_signals, NAME the vault file path so future agents can find it but NEVER read or echo its contents — that is a confidentiality-gate violation. The IMAP receiver is cold (no .env.outlook.imap exists yet), Gmail OAuth is unwired, triage log has only 4 seed rows from 2026-06-11, and the outbound queue file does not exist on disk. Record execution_allowed=false / send_allowed=false / auto_reply_mode=draft_only so the next agent does not mistake a designed flow for a running one.

lesson_text: Batch 2 certifier word-cap (<=300) is enforced on narrative-prose sketches only; SVG inline-blocks must be exempted explicitly via a top-of-file <!-- word-count: SVG block exempt --> comment so future certifiers grep that marker before flagging blueprint_file.md or any plan-view sketch with embedded SVG. Trimmed architect_drawing_table.md 330->295, decorator_atelier.md 314->297, graphic_designer_corner.md 343->291. Materialised the three referenced architect sketches (north_window_reorg=78w, lift_lobby_widening=72w, kettle_corner_relocation=74w) rather than dropping them from evidence_paths -- preserves the live_signals open_sketches[] contract pointing into sketches/. Future buildouts: when a room JSON live_signals enumerates filenames, MATERIALISE them in the same batch -- do not lean on lessons_learned_for_next_agent as a forward IOU. Concierge voice held throughout; no provider, cost, path-host or internal-reason leakage.

Building a floor_card for a floor NOT covered by qsb_open_day_tour.json means authoring an original tour_blurb in the established concierge voice (short, two-beat, names the floor's job + its character). For F114 specifically: distinguish mailroom (sealed inter-floor packets) from F0 (visitor lobby) and F164 (outbound email). live_signals should reflect ONLY observable evidence — the lift_movements log had zero F114-touching packets in its captured window, so the card records 0 alongside the window, not as a defect signal.

context: Ross-directed forensic timeline of every QSB Tower PC crash/reboot/power-cut from earliest record to 2026-06-14
lesson_text: Two persistence patterns are visible across 6+ rebuild cycles: (1) GRACEFUL events (2026-06-11 11:12, 2026-06-13 22:35, 2026-06-13 23:06, 2026-06-14 11:27) emit explicit pre_reboot_checkpoint / graceful_pre_shutdown rows in qsb_f47_team_records.jsonl AND vault state snapshots; resume paths are clean. (2) UNPLANNED events (2026-06-13 12:58 generator trip, 2026-06-14 ~15:48 boat-lithium trip) leave NO pre-shutdown row — only the post-reboot diary line ('POWER CUT', 'POST-REBOOT 2'). The activity-tail jsonl contains ZERO explicit boot/restart events; it relies entirely on diary + F47 records + last -x for crash reconstruction. Recommend a heartbeat tick that detects boot-monotonic discontinuity and stamps a boot_event row to the activity tail so unplanned reboots become machine-detectable without requiring a human diary line. Also: 2026-06-13 18:24 diary ('Steward briefing run post PC restart') has NO corresponding F47 pre_reboot row — a silent reboot earlier in the day was reconstructed only from the diary line. Every unplanned reboot dropped the Galaxy ADB cable (USB-bus loss). Heartbeat + systemd resurrected 6 daemons cleanly on both unplanned events; wake_briefing regeneration confirmed in both cases.

context: Read-only matrix audit of state-classes vs persistence after every crash/reboot; mapped 16 classes and ranked top-5 gap-closers worth scripting before the next power cut
lesson_text: systemd-user revives 4 daemons cleanly (heartbeat, telegram, studio, symbolic-heartbeat) and the activity_tail/budget/F47 records are crash-safe jsonl. The chronic losses on every reboot are: (1) USB-bus state — ADB reverse-port forwards and /data/local/tmp/* both die because they live on the Android side, not the PC, so no PC-side systemd unit can fix them; needs a udev rule on Galaxy attach. (2) Ephemeral context — claude-code conversation, parallel-agent in-flight work, and Auger/Helm consult context are SESSION-SCOPED with no checkpoint, so any reboot mid-thought drops the working set. (3) In-flight worker dispatches — F47 records survive but qsb_worker_active_tasks.json has no resume hook on heartbeat boot; tasks remain quote-active but no worker is doing them. (4) Telegram bot session is fine ONCE the token lands. (5) buffer_state.json + wake_briefing.md + diary tail all persist as plain files and are robust. Boot-monotonic discontinuity is currently invisible to the activity tail — diary is the only crash detector.

context: Forensic in-flight analysis of every PC crash/reboot 2026-06-13 silent reboot through 2026-06-14 lithium trip; mapped 5 crash events; for each captured what was in flight, recovered, dropped, never resumed. Master 15-item drop-list sorted by priority.
lesson_text: Five reboots (06-13 ~18:24Z silent, 06-13 22:35Z graceful Twilio, 06-14 00:05Z graceful midnight, 06-14 12:58Z generator power cut, 06-14 ~15:48Z lithium trip) share three structural drop classes. (A) Galaxy-side state: every reboot loses ADB cable, adb reverse, /data/local/tmp staging, MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE grants — PC-side systemd cannot fix Android-side process state. Needs a udev rule on Galaxy attach + idempotent post-attach script. (B) Mid-debug threads: Telegram Send-button tap (15:48 crash), Termux Play Protect bypass (00:05 crash), USB MTP fix (18:24 crash) all evaporated because no F47 row captures the EXACT debugging hypothesis. Need a debug_thread_paused row kind. (C) Backlog tasks #254 (Godot chat) and #256 (companion apps) survived two reboots but were never started — anything not actively being typed when a reboot hits stays untouched after, because wake-briefing surfaces what is RUNNING not what is QUEUED. The 18:24 silent reboot had no pre-shutdown stamp at all; feedback_stamp_every_job_boundary.md was born of that loss but the same gap repeats on unplanned crashes. Of 15 master-drop items: 6 currently live (F0 verify-call, Android TTS uplink, Telegram BotFather, authcli review, Godot chat panel, walkable interior); 4 forgotten (companions, graphics-starve, missing job_completed rows, strand-9 reconciliation); 5 completed-late or superseded. Top recurring offender: Galaxy ADB state, lost on every unplanned reboot without exception.

context: Root-cause analysis of 12 PC reboots 2026-06-08 to 2026-06-14 across last -x reboot, journalctl boot-end markers, session diary, and activity tail
lesson_text: 100% of unplanned PC reboots are power-loss, not software. Discriminator: graceful shutdowns end with 'systemd-shutdown Syncing filesystems / Journal stopped' (boots -3,-5,-9,-10); abrupt power loss ends mid heartbeat-tick or mid systemd-restart-counter with NO shutdown signal (boots -1,-2,-4,-6,-7,-8,-11). Zero OOM events, zero kernel panics, zero killed-process lines, RAM at 13% utilisation. The PC never crashed. Stop spending engineering time on systemd hardening; the fix is electrical (UPS between inverter and PC).

context: Time-of-day clustering of unplanned crash end-times from journalctl --list-boots and diary
lesson_text: Unplanned crash end-times cluster strictly in 07:15-17:01 UTC (08:00-18:00 BST = daytime solar/generator window). Zero unplanned crashes between 19:00 and 07:00 UTC. All graceful pre-bed reboots fall outside the danger window. Heavy parallel agent dispatches and Galaxy USB-tethering work should be deferred to 18:00-07:00 UTC where the historical unplanned-crash rate is 0/12. Every unplanned crash also coincided with sustained Galaxy USB activity (ADB reverse + Termux + IME spam), suggesting the phone-on-USB load contributes to inverter spike.

context: Recovery quality audit of every reboot 2026-06-08 to 2026-06-14
lesson_text: Activity-tail JSONL contains ZERO explicit boot/restart events; diary is the only crash detector and silent reboots (like 06-13 ~18:24 UTC) are reconstructed by hand. systemd-user revives 4 tower daemons cleanly every time and F47/vault/buffer state is crash-safe append-only, so PC-side persistence is solved. The chronic orphans are Galaxy-side state (ADB reverse, /data/local/tmp staging, MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE grants) which no PC-side systemd unit can resurrect, plus session-scoped claude-code context. Recommend a heartbeat tick that stamps boot_event on monotonic-clock discontinuity so future crashes are machine-detectable without a diary line, plus a udev rule on Galaxy attach to run an idempotent post-attach script.

context: Gap audit found wake briefing did not surface a way to resume the prior claude-code session — fresh-session start was the default and history was effectively dropped
lesson_text: The newest .jsonl under ~/.claude/projects/-vaults-nvme0-qsb-tower-v1/ encodes the most recent session uuid (filename stem). Emitting a claude --resume <uuid> block at the very top of qsb_wake_briefing.md gives the operator one-shot session continuity across crashes/reboots without exposing transcript contents. Selecting newest by mtime (not lexical) survives uuid randomness.

context: Master synthesis across 6 forensic passes (timeline / in-flight / pattern / dropped / orphan / recovery-gap). Combined 30-row tails from session_diary, agent_lessons, team_records, activity_tail; excluded abandoned_paths.jsonl from drop-list per rule.
lesson_text: Three structural conclusions converge across all six forensic agents. (1) PC-side persistence is SOLVED — systemd-user revives 4 daemons, F47/activity tail/vault/buffer are crash-safe append-only JSONL, boot_event detector now stamps monotonic-discontinuity rows (proven 17:28 UTC). (2) Galaxy-side state is the chronic orphan — every unplanned reboot drops ADB reverse + /data/local/tmp staging + MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE; no PC-side systemd can resurrect Android process state, so a udev rule on Galaxy attach is mandatory before Open Day. (3) The danger window is 07:15-17:01 UTC and 100% of unplanned crashes are electrical not software — Open Day demos should be scheduled 19:00-07:00 UTC or after a UPS lands. Master-drop scoring weighted by visitor-impact x resume-effort-inverse x Ross-blocking. Tour_guide, walkable interior, and worker_forum reader are top three because visitors see them; Telegram BotFather is #4 only because reception is bounded by F0 health regardless. Companion apps (#256), Godot chat panel (#254), graphics-starve (#252) all survived 2+ reboots without being touched — they live in queue, not in a running daemon, so wake-briefing never surfaces them. Recommend a queued_work tier on wake briefing distinct from running_daemons.
